q: who invented the first programmable computer
who made the first programmable computer
a: The first programmable computer is generally considered to be the Analytical Engine, designed by Charles Babbage in 1837. Although it was never built during his lifetime, the Analytical Engine contained all the essential elements of a modern computer: an arithmetic logic unit (the mill), control flow through conditional branching and loops, and integrated memory. Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm intended for the Analytical Engine, making her the first computer programmer. The first working programmable computer was the Z3, built by Konrad Zuse in Germany in 1941. It was electromechanical (using relays) and could perform floating-point arithmetic and had a program stored on punched tape. The first electronic general-purpose computer was ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), completed in 1945 at the University of Pennsylvania. It used 18,000 vacuum tubes, weighed 30 tons, and could perform 5,000 additions per second. The first stored-program computer was the Manchester Baby (SSEM) which ran its first program on June 21, 1948. The term bug (computer glitch) was popularized by Grace Hopper who found an actual moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947.
